nodes.text: The application you start with

Pellier's infrastructure, seeded retail data, application, and deployment tools are
provided. Eight marked code sections are unfinished. Complete two in each lab and
check their behavior against independent evidence.

A managed Runtime baseline is also predeployed. Facilitators verify it before the session. Labs 1
and 2 run in the application process; Lab 3 deploys your changes to the managed
path and checks which build actually executed.
Follow a shopper request

A shopper signs in through Cognito. Pellier's dispatcher selects a specialist for
search, recommendation, pricing, inventory, or support. That specialist uses a
bounded set of tools to read or act on business data.

![Pellier's application-process and managed execution paths, with Aurora and the evidence recorded at each boundary.](/workshop-guides/architecture/pellier-governed-overview.svg)

On the managed path, the specialist runs in AgentCore Runtime and reaches published
tools through Gateway. Policy evaluates the caller and tool arguments; permitted
calls reach the Lambda tool implementation and Aurora. Moving execution does not
change which database owns the stock count or order.

Theo and Jessica share a separate staff workflow: a Strands Case Investigator followed by a Resolution Planner. Lab 3 deploys that graph to its own AgentCore Runtime alongside the shopper dispatcher. The backend verifies staff access and retrieves scoped evidence before invoking it with IAM authentication. An assessment can inform a proposal; human approval,
authorization, and execution remain separate steps.
Retrieval, memory, and business state
These capabilities answer different questions:

rows: What products, prices, stock, orders, and returns exist now?
Which catalog candidates match the request's words or meaning?
Reciprocal rank fusion and Cohere Rerank
How should those candidates be combined and ordered?
What was said in a particular conversation?
What context from an earlier conversation might help this request?

nodes.text:
Price and stock predicates determine eligibility. Ranking an over-budget or
sold-out product highly does not make it eligible. Lab 2 checks both ranking
quality and those constraints, by changing the live candidate budget and reading SQL query plans.

Memory has a different role. If Theo said he prefers natural materials, an extracted
preference can guide a later recommendation. The agent must still read Aurora for
current products and availability. A remembered purchase does not prove an order
exists or that a return is permitted.

The Memory experiment starts in Introduction and resumes in Lab 3. Two conversations
share one verified actor; the new conversation has no prior chat events. Ordinary
Storefront threads retain their separate conversation scope.

nodes.text: What makes an action governed?

Sign-in establishes a principal. Cedar authorizes a tool request. Business rules
check the operation's validity. Aurora RLS restricts database access. Operator
adds a human decision boundary for consequential proposals.

A policy ALLOW does not prove execution; a tool attempt does not prove a committed
transaction. Lab 4 correlates attempts with execution and effect records. It checks
a denied key's absence alongside an allowed-key positive control.

The [Appendix](/observatory/guide/reference) provides deeper Memory, identity, and recovery
references. Each lab introduces the commands and checks needed for its own task.

**Start the required path:** [Introduction](/observatory/guide/introduction)
Why the architecture has these boundaries

- Keep SQL eligibility predicates on both retrieval branches, before their limits. A reranker can order candidates; it cannot enforce a missing database predicate or recover a discarded row.
- Keep the shopper and Operator in separate Runtime endpoints. Shopper JWTs reach shopper tools; the backend invokes the Operator graph with IAM. Both execute managed Strands agents after Lab 3.
- Read current business records before graph synthesis, then revalidate approved terms inside the execution transaction. A correct recommendation can become stale before someone approves it.
- Return from the graph before human review. A person’s decision is a durable checkpoint, not an agent waiting in memory.
- Join evidence by exact session, turn, record, and idempotency identifiers. Similar text or nearby timestamps do not prove two records belong to the same action.

nodes.title: Using RDS for PostgreSQL

children.text: The PostgreSQL full-text search, pgvector, JSONB, transaction, and row-security patterns also apply to RDS for PostgreSQL. This workshop uses **RDS Data API with Aurora**. RDS Data API does not support RDS for PostgreSQL DB instances; an adaptation uses native PostgreSQL connections with appropriate networking and pooling. See the [RDS Data API reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rdsdataservice/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html).

nodes.text: 4. Measure - export and check the inventory evidence

Reconcile totals with Marco’s exact turn and run.

```bash
read -r -p 'Turn ID from Why this answer?: ' LAB1_TURN_ID
test -n "$LAB1_TURN_ID"
psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -P pager=off -At \
  -v turn="$LAB1_TURN_ID" -v run="$(cat ~/.pellier/run_id)" \
  -v audit_before="$(cat /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-1-audit-before.txt)" <<'SQL' \
  > /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-1.json
WITH inventory AS (
  SELECT p.product_id,
         p.name,
         p.quantity AS catalog_quantity,
         sum(wi.quantity)::int AS warehouse_quantity,
         (p.quantity - sum(wi.quantity))::int AS inventory_delta
    FROM pellier.product_catalog p
    JOIN pellier.warehouse_inventory wi
      ON wi.product_id = p.product_id
   WHERE p.product_id = '2'
   GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name, p.quantity
),
audit AS (
   SELECT ta.audit_id,
          ta.session_id,
          ta.caller,
          ta.args->>'product_query' AS product_query,
          ta.latency_ms,
          ta.created_at
     FROM pellier.tool_audit ta
     JOIN pellier.governed_turn_receipts gtr
       ON gtr.turn_id = ta.args->>'turn_id'
      AND gtr.session_id = ta.session_id
     JOIN pellier.principal_customers pc
       ON pc.principal_sub = gtr.principal_sub
    WHERE ta.audit_id > :'audit_before'::bigint
      AND ta.tool = 'check_inventory'
      AND ta.run_id = :'run'
      AND gtr.run_id = :'run'
      AND gtr.turn_id = :'turn'
      AND gtr.principal_verified
      AND gtr.terminal_status = 'complete'
      AND gtr.rail = 'in-process'
      AND pc.customer_id = 'CUST-MARCO'
    ORDER BY ta.audit_id
)
SELECT jsonb_pretty(jsonb_build_object(
  'lab', '01-ground-the-answer',
  'runId', :'run',
  'turnId', :'turn',
  'observed', jsonb_build_object(
    'inventory', (SELECT to_jsonb(inventory) FROM inventory),
    'executions', (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(audit)), '[]'::jsonb)
                     FROM audit)
  ),
  'assertions', jsonb_build_object(
    'inventoryReconciled',
      coalesce((SELECT inventory_delta = 0 FROM inventory), false),
    'newInventoryExecution',
      (SELECT count(*) >= 1 FROM audit),
    'newestExecutionNamesTheShirt',
      coalesce((SELECT product_query ILIKE '%hadley%' FROM audit
                 ORDER BY audit_id DESC LIMIT 1), false),
    'executionWasApplicationBound',
      coalesce((SELECT bool_and(caller = 'agent') FROM audit), false)
  )
));
SQL

jq '{observed, assertions}' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-1.json
jq -e '.assertions | [.[]] | all' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-1.json \
  && printf '%s\n' 'Lab 1 PostgreSQL assertions passed'
```

**Expected result:** `Lab 1 PostgreSQL assertions passed`.

**Evidence:** `lab-1.json` binds the inventory comparison to Marco's selected turn
and run. `tool_audit` establishes execution, not Cedar authorization.

nodes.text: 5. Prove - distinguish an unknown product from zero stock

Run the supplied check against your `check_inventory` body. It compares a lookup
with no matching product and the sold-out Quilted Silk Vest:

```bash
cd /workshop/sample-pellier-agentic-search-apg
python3 scripts/lab1_contract_check.py \
  --json /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-1-contract.json
```

**Expected result:** both cases report `PASS`, followed by `PASSED`.
The unknown product returns `not_found` with no stock count. The known product
returns `success`, zero units, and the warehouse results.

nodes.title: Example output and interpretation

children.text:
```text
case       query                    status       total_units  verdict
unknown    Hadley cashmere scarf    not_found    None         PASS
           the catalog does not carry this piece; the agent may say so and nothing about stock
sold_out   Quilted Silk Vest        success      0            PASS
           the catalog carries this piece and every warehouse holds zero; the agent may say it is sold out

What can the agent legitimately conclude in each case?
PASSED
```

`not_found` carries no count, so the agent may say only that the shop does not carry
the piece. `success` with zero units names the piece and every warehouse, so the
agent may say it is sold out. If both read `success`, or both read `not_found`, the
tool body is turning one answer into the other, and the check exits non-zero.

nodes.title: Deep dive - how the retrieval stages differ

children.text:
`pgvector` retrieves by semantic similarity; PostgreSQL full-text search matches
normalized search terms. Aurora returns both ranked lists, then Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines
their positions without comparing incompatible cosine-distance and `ts_rank_cd` scores.

Cohere Rerank reorders the eligible pool with an additional Bedrock model call after
database retrieval. The production question is where that quality gain earns its extra
latency and modeled cost.

children.text:

5. Measure - run the authored worksheet

Restart the backend once after your Python edit, then rerun the same comparison. It uses the Storefront retrieval executor and writes the `observatory-compare` receipt read by the worksheet.

```bash
sudo systemctl restart pellier
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 15 --retry-delay 2 \
  --retry-connrefused localhost:8000/api/health > /dev/null
curl --fail-with-body -sS --get \
  --data-urlencode 'query=A housewarming gift under $100 that is currently in stock.' \
  localhost:8000/api/observatory/search-strategies/compare \
  > /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-comparison.json
for phase in before comparison; do
  jq '{query, sharedQueryEmbeddingObservedMs, strategies:
    [.strategies[] | {strategy, observedMs, modeledCostPerThousandUsd, rerank, extractedFilters, products}]}' \
    "/tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-${phase}.json"
done

jq -n \
  --slurpfile before /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-before.json \
  --slurpfile after /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-comparison.json \
  --arg candidate "$(cat /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-candidate-id.txt)" '
  $before[0] as $b | $after[0] as $a |
  $b.strategies[-1] as $old | $a.strategies[-1] as $new |
  {
    candidateId: $candidate,
    comparisonId: $a.receipt.comparisonId,
    assertions: {
      sameQuery: ($b.query == $a.query),
      savedComparisons: ($b.receipt.persisted == true and $a.receipt.persisted == true
        and ($a.receipt.comparisonId | type) == "string"
        and $b.receipt.comparisonId != $a.receipt.comparisonId),
      starterObserved: ($old.rerank.poolK == 3 and $old.rerank.status == "applied"),
      candidatePreviouslyLost: (
        any($old.rerank.fusedCandidates[]; .productId == $candidate)
        and ($old.rerank.candidateIds | index($candidate)) == null),
      poolExpanded: ($new.rerank.poolK > $old.rerank.poolK
        and ($new.rerank.candidateIds | length) > 3),
      candidateRecovered: (($new.rerank.candidateIds | index($candidate)) != null),
      rerankApplied: ($new.rerank.status == "applied"),
      constraintsPreserved: (
        all([$old, $new][]; .extractedFilters.priceMaxUsd == 100
          and .extractedFilters.inStockOnly == true))
    }
  }' | tee /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-candidates.json
jq -e '.assertions | [.[]] | all' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-candidates.json
```

6. Prove - assert fusion and SQL-enforced eligibility

Select your after request's exact comparison ID, then join the database evidence with the candidate check:

```bash
psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -P pager=off -At \
  -v receipt_high_water="$RECEIPT_HIGH_WATER" \
  -v comparison_id="$(jq -er '.comparisonId' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-candidates.json)" <<'SQL' \
  > /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-database.json
WITH receipt AS (
  SELECT *
    FROM pellier.retrieval_receipts
   WHERE receipt_id > :'receipt_high_water'::bigint
     AND turn_id = :'comparison_id'
     AND retrieval_config->>'source' = 'observatory-compare'
     AND query_preview =
       'A housewarming gift under $100 that is currently in stock.'
   ORDER BY receipt_id DESC
   LIMIT 1
),
returned AS (
  SELECT product_id
    FROM receipt
   CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(citation_ids) AS ids(product_id)
),
violations AS (
  SELECT returned.product_id, p.name, p.price, p.quantity, p.tags
    FROM returned
    LEFT JOIN pellier.product_catalog p USING (product_id)
   WHERE p.product_id IS NULL
      OR p.price > 100
      OR p.quantity <= 0
      OR p.tags ? 'archive'
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT keys.product_id,
         coalesce(1.0 / (
           60 + (r.vector_ranks->>keys.product_id)::int
         ), 0)
         + coalesce(1.0 / (
           60 + (r.lexical_ranks->>keys.product_id)::int
         ), 0) AS recomputed_rrf,
         (r.rrf_scores->>keys.product_id)::numeric AS recorded_rrf
    FROM receipt r
   CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_object_keys(
     r.vector_ranks || r.lexical_ranks
   ) AS keys(product_id)
),
rrf_mismatches AS (
  SELECT *
    FROM ranked
   WHERE recorded_rrf IS NULL
      OR abs(recorded_rrf - recomputed_rrf) > 0.000001
),
assertions AS (
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM receipt) AS receipt_exists,
         EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM returned) AS returned_products_exist,
         coalesce((
           SELECT (hard_constraints->>'price_max_usd')::numeric = 100::numeric
             FROM receipt
         ), false) AS price_constraint_recorded,
         coalesce((
           SELECT (hard_constraints->>'in_stock_only')::boolean
             FROM receipt
         ), false) AS stock_constraint_recorded,
         coalesce((
           SELECT (retrieval_config->>'rerank_pool_k')::int > 3
              AND retrieval_config->>'search_method' = 'hybrid+rerank'
              AND (SELECT count(*) FROM jsonb_object_keys(rerank_scores)) > 3
             FROM receipt
         ), false) AS expanded_rerank_recorded,
         coalesce((
           SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_object_keys(vector_ranks))
              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_object_keys(lexical_ranks))
              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_object_keys(rrf_scores))
             FROM receipt
         ), false) AS hybrid_stages_recorded,
         NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rrf_mismatches) AS rrf_recomputed,
         NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM violations) AS eligibility_enforced
)
SELECT jsonb_pretty(jsonb_build_object(
  'lab', '02-measure-hybrid-retrieval',
  'observed', jsonb_build_object(
    'receipt', (SELECT to_jsonb(receipt) FROM receipt),
    'rerankScores', (SELECT rerank_scores FROM receipt),
    'modeledCostUsd', (SELECT modeled_cost_usd FROM receipt),
    'latencyBreakdown', (SELECT latency_breakdown FROM receipt),
    'eligibilityViolations',
      (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(violations)), '[]'::jsonb)
         FROM violations)
  ),
  'assertions', (SELECT to_jsonb(assertions) FROM assertions)
));
SQL

jq --slurpfile candidates /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-candidates.json '
  .observed.candidateComparison = $candidates[0]
  | .assertions.candidateBuildPassed = ($candidates[0].assertions | [.[]] | all)
' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2-database.json \
  > /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2.json
jq -e '.assertions | [.[]] | all' /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2.json \
  && printf '%s\n' 'Lab 2 PostgreSQL assertions passed'
```

**Evidence:** `/tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-2.json` contains the exact receipt, rerank
scores, modeled cost, latency breakdown, eligibility checks, and recomputed fusion.

nodes.title: Deep dive - why the eligibility distinction matters

children.text:
The model **named** the ceiling; SQL **applied** it. Those are different jobs, and only one
of them is a guarantee.

A reranker reorders what is already allowed. It cannot be relied on to exclude what was
never eligible, because its score is a similarity judgement and eligibility is not a
matter of degree. Had one over-priced row survived into the agentic set, the defect would
be in the predicate rather than in the model's reading of the sentence, and that is the
useful place for it to be: a predicate is testable.

nodes.title: Why issue_credit is published for staff only, and restock not at all

children.text:
Publication adds the tool to the policy action set and to MCP discovery. `issue_credit`
moves money. It is published because the operator desk executes an approved credit
through the Gateway with the operator's own token; its only permit requires the staff
scope claim, no shopper permit names it, and no shopper-facing specialist may bind it.
`restock_inventory` stays deferred until the desk has its own route for it.
`get_ticket_history` is a read scoped to one customer, and Lab 3b is where you make that
scoping true rather than assumed.

**Published is not the same as visible to you.** The Gateway evaluates Cedar on tool
discovery, so an MCP listing returns only what your token could be permitted to call.
For this policy configuration, a shopper token is expected to see 14 of the 16 tools published before this
build and 15 of the 17 after it. Both `issue_credit` and `replace_damaged_item` are staff-only.
A staff token with no customer mapping is expected to see 14: it gains the staff tools
but cannot discover the owner-scoped reads. Compare the actual listing with the source
catalogue for that caller's claims. A published count alone does not prove discovery.

If you deferred the wrong one, the doctor in 3b will tell you.

nodes.title: Actor scope: the experiment and the Storefront differ

children.text:
The cross-session experiment derives one actor from the verified Cognito subject and
an isolated run ID. Both conversations share that actor. Another customer or another
run gets a different actor. Its evidence envelope is stored as a blob event in
AgentCore; it is not an Aurora transaction receipt.

Regular Storefront conversations use `user-{sub}-session-{sid}` as their actor.
Their preference namespace is `/pellier/preferences/user-{sub}-session-{sid}/`.
Starting a new Storefront conversation therefore does not retrieve another
conversation's extracted preferences. This experiment demonstrates an explicit
alternative without changing that isolation policy.

For cross-session continuity in production, choose a stable authenticated actor,
separate session IDs, and namespace permissions that enforce ownership. Retention,
correction, and deletion rules are also application design choices.

```bash
psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -P pager=off -At \
  -v session="$SESSION" <<'SQL' \
  > /tmp/pellier-evidence/lab-3-database.json
WITH receipt AS (
  SELECT *
    FROM pellier.governed_turn_receipts
   WHERE session_id = :'session'
   ORDER BY created_at DESC
   LIMIT 1
),
thread AS (
  SELECT *
    FROM pellier.governed_turn_receipts
   WHERE session_id = :'session'
   ORDER BY created_at
),
thread_retrieval AS (
  SELECT r.*
    FROM thread t
    JOIN pellier.retrieval_receipts r
      ON r.receipt_id = t.retrieval_receipt_id
)
SELECT jsonb_pretty(jsonb_build_object(
  'sessionId', :'session',
  'turnReceipt', (SELECT to_jsonb(receipt) FROM receipt),
  'threadReceipts', (
    SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(thread)), '[]'::jsonb)
      FROM thread
  ),
  'threadRetrievalReceipts', (
    SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(thread_retrieval)), '[]'::jsonb)
      FROM thread_retrieval
  ),
  'assertions', jsonb_build_object(
    'receiptExists', EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM receipt),
    'threeManagedTurns', (
      SELECT count(*) >= 3 AND bool_and(
        terminal_status = 'complete' AND principal_verified AND rail = 'gateway-mcp'
      ) FROM thread
    ),
    'threadRetrievalReceipt', EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM thread_retrieval),
    'verifiedPrincipal',
      coalesce((SELECT principal_verified FROM receipt), false),
    'managedGatewayRail',
      coalesce((SELECT rail = 'gateway-mcp' FROM receipt), false),
    'managedRuntime',
      coalesce((SELECT trace->>'runtime' = 'agentcore-managed' FROM receipt), false),
    'runtimeRequestCorrelated',
      coalesce((SELECT length(trace->>'runtimeRequestId') > 0 FROM receipt), false),
    'serviceEvidence',
      coalesce((SELECT trace->>'evidenceProvenance' = 'agentcore-service-telemetry'

));
```

nodes.title: Where `execution_receipts` fits, and why absence alone is not enough

children.text:
`pellier.execution_receipts` is the append-only companion the application writes on the
operator path: **one row per attempt**, carrying the policy verdict, what Aurora did, and
what proves it. The direct Gateway calls in this required path do not pass through that
operator workflow, so they do not create those rows.

Absence is fragile evidence on its own. This lab uses a unique idempotency key, preserves
the exact AgentCore CLI response, classifies only explicit policy-enforcement text, and
queries the matching execution and write rows by that key. That is a bounded workshop
proof. The CLI files are not provider decision events, and they do not contain a
provider invocation ID or authoritative policy version or hash.

```sql

  FROM pellier.execution_receipts ORDER BY receipt_id DESC LIMIT 5;
```

proofs below go straight through your bearer token with no human review step. It fills on
the separately authenticated Operator workflow. The required Operator close later in this
lab inspects that boundary without turning the direct CLI proof into an approval.

These are independent tests. The Gateway denial never reaches Aurora; the RLS

nodes.title: Why a role can be scoped by a mapping it cannot read

children.text:
`REVOKE ALL ON pellier.principal_customers FROM pellier_query` is in migration
`016_runtime_roles_rls.sql`: neither runtime role can read the mapping table, or
enumerate who else exists in it. The scoping still works because of two
properties:

- **The resolver is `SECURITY DEFINER`.**
  `pellier.current_principal_customers()` executes as its owner, with
  `SET search_path = pg_catalog, pellier` pinned, so it can read the mapping
  on behalf of a caller that cannot. The RLS policy calls only this function -
  it never reads the table directly.
- **`pellier.principal_sub` is a transaction-local setting.** The application
  derives it from the verified identity before querying protected rows.
  RLS evaluates it through the resolver.

RLS trusts that application-supplied setting; it does not verify a Cognito token.
The worksheet sets it directly to test database policy. A production query
interface must prevent callers from choosing or changing that setting.

The application sets the role and then the principal in the protected
transaction. The worksheet resolves the subject before the role switch because
the runtime roles deliberately cannot enumerate the mapping table.

One more detail matters: the policy names **both** runtime roles. One that named
only the agent role would leave model-generated SQL running as `pellier_query`
unfiltered.

nodes.title: The one expression both clauses delegate to

children.text:
`orders_principal_scope` and `returns_principal_scope` each set `USING` and
`WITH CHECK` to the same test:

```sql
customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM pellier.current_principal_customers())
```

The read filter and write guard share the same ownership test. That function resolves the
transaction-local `pellier.principal_sub` through the mapping table, and it is
`STABLE SECURITY DEFINER` with a pinned `search_path` so a runtime role that cannot
read the mapping can still be scoped by it.

The security-relevant consequence: the function is set-returning, so a mapping row
that gave one subject two customers would widen *every* policy at once. Migration
`038_principal_customer_cardinality.sql` is the durable guarantee: it first refuses an
already ambiguous database, then enforces `UNIQUE (principal_sub)`. The seeder performs
the same check before it writes, giving provisioning a clear failure rather than relying
on the database error alone. `customer_id` is intentionally not unique, because one
customer may legitimately have multiple authenticated logins.

nodes.title: Why a receipt cannot prove its own absence, and why the fifth count is the control

children.text:
A Cedar DENY receipt records that the Gateway refused Marco's call for Jessica's return.
It cannot prove that nothing ran. A receipt records a decision, not an effect, so only
the tables an execution would have written can settle that. Each denied count rules out a different failure: the
tool ran and the receipt is wrong, a write was claimed before anything refused it, a write
finished, stock moved.

Four zeros can also result from querying the wrong key or environment. The same
query must find exactly one finalized write for Jessica's allowed key. This
positive control makes the absence result interpretable.

Open `workshop/lab-4-absence.sql`, search for `deny proof`, and replace
the five `NULL::bigint` placeholders with scalar subqueries over the tables above, using
`:'deny_key'` and `:'allow_key'`.

nodes.title: Optional - tie the investigation to the exact write key in SQL

children.text:
Keep customer Jessica, staff principal `operator`, Cedar authorization, RLS enforcement,
and human review distinct. The direct AgentCore CLI proof had no approval record.

```bash
psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -P pager=off \
  -v allow_key="$ALLOW_KEY" <<'SQL'
SELECT c.session_id,
       m.metadata->>'turn_id' AS operator_turn_id,
       m.metadata->'artifact'->'orchestration'->>'pattern' AS pattern,
       m.metadata->'artifact'->'orchestration'->>'execution' AS execution,
       m.metadata->'artifact'->'orchestration'->'executedNodes'
         AS executed_nodes
  FROM pellier.conversations c
  JOIN pellier.messages m USING (session_id)
 WHERE c.agent_name = 'operator_concierge'
   AND c.metadata->>'customer_id' = 'CUST-JESSICA'
   AND m.role = 'assistant'
   AND m.metadata->'artifact'->'orchestration' IS NOT NULL
 ORDER BY m.id DESC
 LIMIT 1;

SELECT ta.audit_id,
       ta.tool,
       ta.caller,
       ta.args->>'customer_id' AS requested_customer,
       ta.args->>'idempotency_key' AS idempotency_key,
       wo.operation,
       wo.completed_at,
       wo.result
  FROM pellier.tool_audit ta
  JOIN pellier.write_operations wo
    ON wo.idempotency_key = ta.args->>'idempotency_key'
 WHERE ta.args->>'idempotency_key' = :'allow_key';

SELECT r.id AS return_id,
       r.customer_id,
       r.product_id,
       r.reason,
       r.status,
       r.requested_at
  FROM pellier.returns r
 WHERE r.customer_id = 'CUST-JESSICA'
 ORDER BY r.requested_at DESC, r.id DESC;
SQL
```

The graph artifact records observable model work. Execution rows prove the Gateway
effect; the Operator session proves a separately authenticated staff investigation.

Creating a consequential proposal requires an explicit request and is optional here.
CLI policy receipts carry the current workshop run. A recent row from another run
cannot establish this participant's result.

nodes.text: Aurora and AgentCore Memory

Aurora is the authority for business state. AgentCore Memory preserves conversation
context and extracts information that may help future requests. Treat retrieved
Memory text as context to evaluate, not as trusted instructions or permission.

nodes.text:
An AgentCore `SEMANTIC` record might say that a shopper plans a trip. A
`USER_PREFERENCE` record might say that they prefer linen. Both are derived from
conversation. Neither proves that an order exists. An AgentCore `EPISODIC` record
summarizes an interaction and its assessed outcome; it is not the authoritative
order or return ledger.
What the required Memory experiment establishes

Introduction records Theo's supplied first conversation. While participants build
Labs 1 and 2, AgentCore extracts facts, preferences, and a summary. Lab 3 retrieves
records into a new conversation with no prior chat events, invokes current catalog tools, and preserves
the record IDs used by that answer. Participants identify a remembered preference
in the answer and verify a recommended product against Aurora.

The experiment uses one actor derived from a verified Cognito subject and a run ID.
The conversations have distinct session IDs under that actor. Ordinary Storefront conversations
still use `user-{sub}-session-{sid}` as their actor; they do not share extracted
preferences across conversations. Choose actor continuity deliberately in a production
application, and enforce namespace access as well as authentication.

The required experiment uses `SEMANTIC`, `USER_PREFERENCE`, and `SUMMARIZATION`
records. Its source also configures `EPISODIC`; consolidation is optional during the

For production use, define retention, correction and deletion behavior, and how an
explicit new request supersedes an old preference. Test isolation with a different
verified principal. A namespace naming convention by itself is not an authorization
policy.

nodes.title: System and governance reference

children.text:
Pellier is a retail story wrapped around four engineering questions: **what is true, how was it found, what ran, and what changed**.

![Identity, execution, authorization, data, and evidence each form a separate boundary.](/workshop-guides/introduction/governance-layers.svg)

rows: shopper conversation and grounded product response
product cards and emitted tool evidence
optional visual lens over a live shopper turn
separate staff investigation and service recovery
human review, action status, and receipts

children.text: One policy engine is not governance
Cedar decides whether a caller may invoke a protected tool. It does not replace database ownership checks, constraints, or evidence required to reconstruct the attempt.
Policy receipt: was the action permitted?

`pellier.governed_receipts` records the JWT-bound principal, tool, arguments, policy
name, the Gateway helper's `ALLOW` or policy-enforcement `DENY` classification, and the
keyed execution check. It is strong workshop evidence, but it is not a provider decision
event. A production-grade authorization receipt also needs the provider invocation ID,
policy version or hash, and authoritative decision-event source.
Execution receipt: what actually ran?
`pellier.execution_receipts` records an attempt across Runtime and Gateway, including attempts that Aurora refuses. `pellier.tool_audit` records a tool call that reaches the application boundary.
Data receipt: what reached Aurora?

`pellier.write_operations`, the domain row, and `pellier.inventory_ledger` show resulting business state. A replay may create a second attempt receipt but no second durable effect.

Row-Level Security is enabled for shopper-scoped `orders` and `returns`. Runtime roles use `NOBYPASSRLS`; narrowly scoped `SECURITY DEFINER` functions cross an otherwise hidden principal mapping boundary.

Do not replace `tool_audit` with pgAudit. Tool audit is application-level evidence correlated to a turn; pgAudit and PostgreSQL logs are complementary statement-level evidence.

CloudWatch carries runtime and application signals. CloudTrail records AWS control-plane
activity. The optional `advanced_verified_customer_context.dogwood` example goes beyond
the baseline `baseline_permit_gateway_tools` rule. The workshop joins its Gateway
attempts with stable session and idempotency keys. Treat a provider-issued invocation
identity as the production target; do not infer one from a high-water mark or a missing
row.
Boundary with Mosaic

Pellier assumes a working hybrid retrieval layer and concentrates on managed execution, tools, authorization, and proof. Mosaic is the companion deep dive for retrieval mechanics and evaluation; neither workshop substitutes for the other.

nodes.text: Set up your steering file

In Code Editor, create **`CLAUDE.local.md` at the source repository root**. Copy
the [partly completed coaching template](/workshop-guides/coach/CLAUDE.local.md) into it.
Keep the existing `CLAUDE.md` files. The local file adds your current exercise and
prediction to the repository's guidance.

Fill its four fields from the lab: **build, allowed file/marker, prediction, and
acceptance command**. Change these fields for each build. For Lab 1, list both
allowed files if you work on 1a and 1b together.

nodes.title: Tip: make your prediction testable

children.text:
“The SQL should work” is hard to test. “A candidate found by only one search branch
should receive one contribution, and the saved score should match within the
worksheet's tolerance” gives your coach something precise to question.

nodes.text: Start in Plan mode

From the source repository root:

```bash
cd /workshop/sample-pellier-agentic-search-apg
claude --permission-mode plan
```

Inside Claude Code, use `/status` to confirm Bedrock and the configured model, then
`/memory` to confirm that `CLAUDE.local.md` is loaded. Paste the prompt from your
lab's **Claude Code coach** tab.

Plan mode supports inspection and planning before source edits. When you are ready,
ask for the smallest proposed patch. You can apply it yourself, or switch to the
normal permission mode and review each proposed edit. Use `/exit` before running the
lab's commands in the terminal.

The steering file describes behavior; it is not a security boundary. Review the file
scope and diff yourself. Keep normal permission prompts enabled. See Anthropic's
[project memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) and
[permission modes](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) documentation.

nodes.text:
If the proposed edit changes tests, tool grants outside the exercise, or unrelated
files, reject that edit and restate the scope. If one attempt does not converge by the
lab's checkpoint time, use **Catch up**. The goal is understanding the boundary, not
debugging a coding assistant.

nodes.title: Recovery: Claude asks for a personal login or cannot call a model

children.text:
Do not paste AWS credentials into the conversation or change the account setup.
Open a fresh Code Editor terminal and try once more: the workshop shell loads the
Bedrock environment. If `/status` still shows the wrong provider, switch to manual
editing and ask a facilitator to check the CLI installation, model access, and instance
role. [Claude Code on Bedrock](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock) documents
the provider setup used by the workshop.

nodes.title: Recovery: the coach follows the previous lab or tries to solve everything

children.text:
Exit, update the four fields in `CLAUDE.local.md`, and start a fresh Plan-mode session.
Name the current build and paste only its bounded prompt. Do not carry a broad
“finish the workshop” instruction between exercises.
